recipe:agents-why-each-element-of-a-desi.stdout:
Roof: from flat tiles to a working roof

Requirements:
  R1: keep the design rain out of the room [lap_water_ingress]
  R2: no condensation dripping into the room [underside_condensation]
  R3: no radiant discomfort from the ceiling on a sunny day [radiant_heat_gain]

Version 0 (tiles):
  rain ingress through the lap fails: Water climbs the 1 mm gap of the lap by capillarity up to 14 mm, the wind pushes it 6.15 mm further and with no slope nothing drives the water off: the design storm ponds 25 mm: the total head (14 + 6.15 + 25 = 45.1 mm) exceeds the 0 mm the 75 mm lap rises at 0°. Water gets over the lap and drips inside.
  [proof: capillary + wind + film head 45.1 mm > height the lap rises 0 mm; hydraulic barrier of a lapped joint: capillary rise between plates + wind head + Nusselt film / ponding vs lap rise]
  Options tried:
    - increase_slope: fixes (margin -1 -> 0.358), cost: +7.9 % roof area (index 0.079)
    - longer_lap: infeasible (with no slope no lap lifts the water (L sin 0 = 0))
  So: pitch the roof to the material's minimum slope — gravity now drains the water (thin film instead of a pond) and the lap gains height (L sin(alpha)) against capillarity and wind
  -> slope_deg = 22.0
  (chosen: fixes the failure without breaking any requirement that passed)

Version 1 (tiles, pitch):
  condensation under the roof fails: On a clear night the tile radiates to the sky at -1.74 °C and cools to 14.2 °C; the tile underside, in contact with the room air, sits at 14.9 °C, below the dew point of the room air (16.4 °C at 21 °C and 75 %): vapour condenses and drips into the room.
  [proof: dew point of the room air 16.4 °C > temperature of the surface facing the room 14.9 °C; steady roof heat-balance network (clear night) + Magnus dew point]
  Options tried:
    - ceiling_ventilated_attic: fixes (margin -0.316 -> 0.37), cost: 1 m^2 of ceiling per m^2 of plan (index 1.5)
    - ceiling_insulation: infeasible (needs first: ceiling)
  So: ceiling with a ventilated attic — room air no longer touches the cold (or hot) tile: a ventilated attic and the ceiling sit in between, and the ceiling, fed by the tile's radiation, faces the room much closer to the air temperature
  (chosen: fixes the failure without breaking any requirement that passed)

Version 2 (tiles, pitch, ceiling):
  radiant heat gain from the roof fails: The 900 W/m^2 sun heats the tile to 59.1 °C; the ceiling above the occupants sits at 39 °C, 12 K above the room air (27 °C), more than the 5 K of radiant asymmetry acceptable for a warm ceiling: it pours 78.7 W/m^2 into the room.
  [proof: ceiling radiant asymmetry 12.0 K > comfort limit (warm ceiling) 5 K; steady roof heat-balance network (clear day, sun on the roof)]
  Options tried:
    - ceiling_ventilated_attic: infeasible (the concept already has 'ceiling')
    - radiant_barrier: fixes (margin -1.402 -> 0.482), cost: 1 m^2 of foil per m^2 of roof (index 0.4)
    - ceiling_insulation: fixes (margin -1.402 -> 0.438), cost: 50 mm of mineral wool on the ceiling (index 0.4)
  So: radiant barrier (low-emissivity foil under the tiles) — the tile underside gets an emissivity of ~0.05: tile-to-ceiling radiation, the dominant path, drops by an order of magnitude
  -> tile_under_emissivity = 0.05
  (chosen: fixes the failure without breaking any requirement that passed; of 2 options that fix it, it is the cheapest (0.4, 3 checks passing; vs ceiling_insulation: 3 passing, cost 0.4))

Version 3 (tiles, pitch, ceiling, radiant barrier):
  Every requirement passes.
  - R1/lap_water_ingress: 20.7 <= 28.1 mm
  - R2/underside_condensation: 16.4 <= 19.2 °C
  - R3/radiant_heat_gain: 2.591 <= 5 K
